question: What is the main idea behind Dorothea Orem's nursing theory?

options.A: The pharmacological management of chronic infectious diseases
options.B: The strict hierarchy of hospital administration and ward management
options.C: The reduction of hospital expenditure through short-stay admissions
options.D: The importance of patient self-care and independent health maintenance

explanation: Orem focused her theory on a simple truth: people need to practice deliberate self-care to stay healthy and live well! [learn more](BMP110_U3_T8#BMP110_U3_T8_h1)

question: How does Dorothea Orem describe 'self-care' in her model?

options.A: Emergency interventions required only during acute traumatic injuries or sudden surgery
options.B: Medical treatments prescribed by a physician and administered strictly by a registered nurse
options.C: Learned, purposeful actions that individuals perform on their own behalf to maintain well-being
options.D: Automatic biological reflexes that regulate body temperature and blood pressure without thought

explanation: Self-care isn't automatic! It's something we learn and intentionally do to support our own health and growth. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T8#BMP110_U3_T8_h1)

question: In Orem's theory, what does the term 'self-care agency' mean?

options.A: A government ministry responsible for regulating nursing practice
options.B: An acute medical emergency requiring immediate hospital admission
options.C: The financial cost of purchasing medications at a local pharmacy
options.D: The acquired human ability or power to engage in self-care

explanation: Think of 'agency' as a person's learned power or ability to take care of themselves effectively. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T8#BMP110_U3_T8_h2)

question: According to Orem, when do we actually need professional nursing care?

options.A: When the patient refuses to take prescribed oral medications at home
options.B: When the doctor fails to document the daily ward round notes
options.C: When the hospital runs out of basic medical supplies and consumables
options.D: When the therapeutic self-care demand is greater than the patient's self-care agency

explanation: In plain words: nurses step in when a patient's health needs are bigger than what they can manage on their own right now. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T8#BMP110_U3_T8_h2)

question: What is a 'self-care deficit' in Orem's theory?

options.A: A shortage of qualified nurses working in a rural health center
options.B: The financial inability to pay hospital bills in a private clinic
options.C: An inequality where self-care demands are greater than the person's agency
options.D: A complete absence of universal biological needs in human beings

explanation: A deficit simply means there's a gap: the patient needs more care than they are currently able to provide for themselves. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T8#BMP110_U3_T8_h3)

question: A patient is admitted with a severe stroke, weakness on one side, and trouble swallowing. According to Orem, what does this show?

options.A: A high level of self-care agency requiring health education
options.B: A universal self-care requisite that needs no professional help
options.C: A clear self-care deficit requiring nursing intervention
options.D: A supportive-educative nursing system requirement only

explanation: Because the patient's body won't let them handle basic needs right now, they have a self-care deficit and need our nursing hands! [learn more](BMP110_U3_T8#BMP110_U3_T8_h3)

question: Which nursing system fits best for a patient who is unconscious in the intensive care unit?
explanation: 'Wholly' means completely! Since an unconscious patient can't do anything for themselves, the nurse compensates entirely. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T8#BMP110_U3_T8_h4)

question: What happens in a supportive-educative nursing system?

options.A: The nurse performs all physical care while the patient remains completely passive in bed
options.B: The family members live in the hospital ward to feed and bathe the patient
options.C: The physician takes over both nursing duties and patient education entirely
options.D: The patient can perform self-care with guidance, instruction, and support from the nurse

explanation: Here, the patient is capable! They just need teaching, encouragement, and guidance from us to succeed. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T8#BMP110_U3_T8_h4)

question: How can Nigerian midwives and nurses best include family members using Orem's model?

options.A: By restricting all visitors to prevent them from interfering with hospital routines
options.B: By delegating all professional nursing assessments to visiting relatives
options.C: By involving relatives to help meet the patient's therapeutic self-care demands
options.D: By asking family members to pay all hospital bills before treatment starts

explanation: Family is a huge strength in our culture! Relatives helping with basic care fits wonderfully into supportive nursing care. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T8#BMP110_U3_T8_h5)

question: A nurse teaches a busy clinic patient with high blood pressure how to cut down on salt using local foods. Which nursing system is this?
explanation: Teaching and guiding a patient to manage their own diet is the heart of the supportive-educative system. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T8#BMP110_U3_T8_h5)

question: What is one of the biggest strengths of Dorothea Orem's theory?

options.A: It requires zero documentation or clinical assessment from the nurse
options.B: It promotes patient independence, empowerment, and active involvement in care
options.C: It eliminates the need for any collaboration between doctors and nurses
options.D: It guarantees that patients will never experience chronic illnesses or pain

explanation: Orem's model helps patients become the bosses of their own health by encouraging independence and teamwork with the nurse. [learn more](BMP110_U3_T8#BMP110_U3_T8_h6)

question: What is a known limitation of applying Orem's theory in everyday practice?

options.A: It assumes every patient desires and can achieve complete self-care independence
options.B: It requires expensive laboratory equipment to calculate a self-care deficit
options.C: It forbids nurses from ever teaching patients about their prescribed medications
options.D: It applies exclusively to pediatric patients and cannot be used for adults

explanation: Not every patient wants or is able to be completely independent, especially when very sick or due to cultural preferences! [learn more](BMP110_U3_T8#BMP110_U3_T8_h6)
